claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between thermodynamic driving forces for phase separation and diffusion-controlled kinetic limitations.
Composition-dependent thermodynamic instability is the structural mediator of phase stability.
Diffusion limitations counter thermodynamic driving forces for phase separation.
The balance between thermodynamic driving forces and diffusion limitations determines phase stability.
Isothermal holding at lower temperatures will cause phase separation because thermodynamic driving forces dominate.
Within the tested sub-high-temperature regime, relatively higher temperatures will maintain a stable BCC phase because kinetic limitations prevail.
Vacuum or an inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during isothermal holding.
The exact temperature dependence of the competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors is unknown.
